prompt: Why is a signup form and a credit card not enough to hand a company an API key to Tarefa's assistant?
hint: Whose account does somebody abusing a model prefer to use?

choices.text: Credit cards cannot be charged for usage that is billed per token
choices.why: Billing per token works with a card; the problem is who is behind it.

choices.text: The LGPD forbids opening an account without a CNPJ
choices.why: There is no such rule; the checks are Tarefa's choice.

choices.text: Abusers want an account in someone else's name
choices.why: Right: an API that hands keys to any card becomes that account.

choices.text: A form cannot collect the company's website address
choices.why: It can; the question is what the form's answers prove.

prompt: What does a CNPJ with correct check digits prove?
hint: The digits are computed from the twelve before them.

choices.text: That the number was not mistyped, nothing more than that
choices.why: Right: the registry is the next check.

choices.text: That the company exists and is active at the Receita
choices.why: That needs the registry; the arithmetic only says the number is well formed.

choices.text: That the contact address belongs to the company
choices.why: The check digits say nothing about an e-mail address.

choices.text: That the company has been open for more than six months
choices.why: The opening date comes from the registry, not from the digits.

prompt: Match each application to the reason the lab gave first.
hint: One reason on the right was given to nobody.

pairs.right: Contact address is not at the company's domain

prompt: Nuvem Tradutora's contact uses a webmail address instead of the company's domain. Why does the lab answer VERIFY and a sandbox, not a refusal?
hint: Is this a sign of fraud or something easy to fix?

choices.text: The rule against webmail addresses applies to new companies
choices.why: No such rule exists in the lab; the age check is separate.

choices.text: Translation is an allowed use, which overrides the other checks
choices.why: A prohibited use or a bad CNPJ would still refuse it.

choices.text: A webmail address does not receive the key once it is issued
choices.why: They can receive mail like any other address.

choices.text: A weak signal, fixed by confirming an address at the domain
choices.why: Right: the signal decides how much it starts with, and the fix is cheap.

prompt: Of the eight applications, how many did the lab accept straight to tier-1?
What separates a use case on the review list from one on the allowed list?
hint: Who is hurt when the model is wrong?

choices.text: Review uses cost more tokens per request
choices.why: Cost has nothing to do with the lists.

choices.text: A failure lands on somebody who never chose the model
choices.why: Right: a candidate, a patient, a party to a contract.

choices.text: Review uses are prohibited unless the company pays more
choices.why: They are not prohibited, and price buys nothing here.

choices.text: Allowed uses are the ones the provider has tested itself
choices.why: The lists are Tarefa's policy, not a record of the provider's tests.

prompt: Which of these use cases are on the lab's prohibited list? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Sending bulk messages to people who never asked for them
choices.why: Yes: `mass-messaging`.

choices.text: Writing fake reviews
choices.why: Yes: `fake-reviews`.

choices.text: Tracking an individual
choices.why: Yes: `tracking-individuals`.

choices.text: Screening job applicants
choices.why: That is `hiring-screening`, on the review list.

choices.text: Answering patients' questions about symptoms
choices.why: That is `health-information`, on the review list.

prompt: Avalia+ Marketing chose the category `marketing-copy`. Why does the lab read its free-text description as well?

choices.text: The applicant picks the category, so it is easy to fake
choices.why: Right: the sentence said 5-star reviews.

choices.text: Categories are often misspelt, and the description corrects them
choices.why: The category comes from a list; the problem is honesty, not spelling.

choices.text: The description is what is sent to the model on every call
choices.why: It is part of the application, not of any request.

choices.text: Marketing copy is prohibited unless the description says otherwise
choices.why: It is on the review list, not the prohibited one.

prompt: Contrata Já RH wants to "reject the weakest automatically". Which outcome does the lesson call reasonable?
hint: Who reads a rejected CV in their plan?

choices.text: Approval exactly as written, since hiring-screening is already on the review list
choices.why: Being on the review list means a person decides; it is not an approval.

choices.text: Refusal of every hiring use, since art. 20 bans automated decisions
choices.why: Art. 20 gives a right to review; it does not ban the decision.

choices.text: Approval without the automatic rejections, with a recruiter reviewing every ranking
choices.why: Right: or a refusal; what is not reasonable is approving the sentence as written.

choices.text: Approval at tier-2 straight away, so the volume of CVs fits
choices.why: Nobody starts at tier-2; it needs sixty clean days and a review.

prompt: Put the review of an application in order.
hint: A decision is the last thing, and it is written down.
items: Check the company: CNPJ, registry, domain
Read the declared use case against the policy lists
Ask who the end users are and whether a person acts on the output
Decide, and record the decision with the reviewer's name and reason

prompt: Why does an accepted customer start at tier-1 and not at the largest tier?
hint: What bounds the damage a key can do?

choices.text: Providers charge less for small tiers, and the saving goes to the customer
choices.why: Price is not the reason for the tiers.

choices.text: Tier-2 is reserved for companies opened more than ten years ago
choices.why: Tier-2 needs a clean history at tier-1, whatever the company's age.

choices.text: Larger tiers need a second CNPJ to be registered
choices.why: One CNPJ; what tier-2 needs is time and a review.

choices.text: This key has no history, and its allowance bounds its damage
choices.why: Right: trust is earned with sixty clean days and a review.

prompt: In week 2026-W36, what percentage of Doce Lar's requests fell outside its declared use case?
Doce Lar's drift is flagged. Why does the lesson start the response by asking rather than suspending?
hint: Where did the topic labels come from?

choices.text: A suspension is only allowed after three warnings under the LGPD
choices.why: The LGPD sets no such rule; the ladder is Tarefa's policy.

choices.text: The topics come from a classifier, which mislabels some descriptions
choices.why: Right: asking costs a message, and a wrong suspension costs a customer.

choices.text: Fake reviews are allowed if the customer pays for tier-2
choices.why: They are prohibited at every tier.

choices.text: The drift limit of 30% is a legal threshold that the ANPD has set for providers
choices.why: It is the lab's choice, written down with its reason.

prompt: Which signals in `guard drift` point at a change in what Doce Lar does? Choose all that apply.
hint: There are two, and they agree.

choices.text: The share outside the use case climbs from 5% to 79%
choices.why: Yes: the key is now mostly doing something else.

choices.text: The weekly volume more than quadruples in two weeks
choices.why: Yes: from 2,240 to 9,800.

choices.text: The CNPJ status changes from ATIVA to INAPTA
choices.why: The drift report does not read the registry; nothing says the status changed.

choices.text: The contact address moves to a webmail domain
choices.why: Nothing in the usage log says anything about the contact.

prompt: When the answer is pending, a customer whose use is in question can be moved back to the ___, where nothing reaches end users.
Match each decision the lab can print to what follows from it.
hint: One consequence on the right belongs to no decision.

pairs.right: The sandbox until a person approves the use case
The sandbox until a cheap signal is fixed
No key, with every reason listed

right_distractors: A key at tier-2 at once

prompt: An applicant declares `translation` and writes "translate our product testimonials into Portuguese". The lab accepts it. What does the lesson say about that?
hint: What would the phrase list need to have seen?

choices.text: The acceptance is final, since translation is on the allowed list
choices.why: Nothing is final: drift checks what the key actually does afterwards.

choices.text: The phrase list has holes, and drift catches what it lets through
choices.why: Right: the word testimonials is on no list, and usage will show what the key does.

choices.text: Translation should be moved to the prohibited list
choices.why: Translating is a legitimate use; the risk is in what is translated.

choices.text: The applicant should have been refused for writing in English
choices.why: The language of the application has nothing to do with the decision.
